statement.name: Least upper bound principle
statement.definition: For second-order phi(x^1) extensional on R with phi(0) and not phi(1), there is a least y in [0,1] such that phi(z) fails for all z in (y,1].
statement.facts: Theorem 4.2: RCA0^omega proves (exists^3) -> LUB -> HBU.

statement.name: Uniform Heine's theorem for Cantor space
statement.definition: (forall G^2)(exists m^0)(forall F^2)[MPC(F,G) -> (forall f,g in C)(f m = g m -> F(f)=F(g))], where G is a modulus of pointwise continuity for F.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.23: RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} proves UCTu <-> HBUc (QF-AC^{0,1} removable in favour of IND); equivalent to HBU and PITu.

statement.name: Uniform Heine's theorem for the unit interval
statement.definition: For any eps > 0 and g : I x R -> R+, there is delta > 0 such that every f : I -> R with modulus of continuity g satisfies |x-y|<delta -> |f(x)-f(y)|<eps.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.27: RCA0^omega + WKL proves UCTRu <-> FEJu; Corollary 4.28: RCA0^omega + WKL + QF-AC^{0,1} proves UCTRu <-> FEJu <-> HBU.

statement.name: Uniform Fejer's theorem
statement.definition: For any k and g : I_pi x R -> R+ there is N such that every f : I_pi -> R with modulus of continuity g and f(0)=0 has Cesaro means sigma_n(f,x) converging to f within 1/k uniformly for n>=N and |sigma_n(f,y)| <= nN.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.27 and Corollary 4.28 (see UCTRu).

statement.name: Pincherle's theorem without a realiser for local boundedness
statement.definition: (forall F^2)[(forall f in C)(exists n)(forall g in C)(g in [f n] -> F(g) <= n) -> (exists m)(forall h in C)(F(h) <= m)].
statement.facts: PITo <-> PIT'o <-> WKL over RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}; Z_2^omega does not prove it (Corollary 4.12 remark); LGP implies it.

statement.name: Pincherle's theorem for sub-continuous functions
statement.definition: A sub-continuous function on Cantor space is bounded.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.22: Z_2^omega cannot prove it, while RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} proves WKL <-> PIT''o.

statement.name: Pincherle's theorem for Baire space
statement.definition: (forall F^2,G^2)[LOCb(F,G) -> (exists H^2 in cont)(forall g^1)(F(g) <= H(g))].
statement.facts: PITb + WKL implies PITo; PITb has no first-order strength; LIND(N^N) with (exists^2) proves PITb.

statement.name: Local-to-global principle
statement.definition: For L_2-formulas A(f,n) with type two parameters, increasing in n: (forall f in C)(exists n)(forall g in [f n])A(g,n) -> (exists m)(forall h in C)A(h,m).
statement.facts: Theorem 4.18: RCA0^omega + LGP + IND proves HBU; LGP implies PIT'o; the variant LGP^- (no type two parameters) is provable in Z_2^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} (Corollary 4.19).

statement.name: Borel-Schoenflies Lindelof lemma for the reals
statement.definition: For every open covering of R provided by Psi : C -> Q^2 there is Phi : N -> C with (forall x in R)(exists n)(x in J^Psi_{Phi(n)}).
statement.facts: Theorem 5.2: RCA0^omega + LINDbs proves WKL <-> PITo; Theorem 5.3: RCA0^omega + LINDbs proves QF-AC^{0,1}_R; Corollary 5.4: ZF does not prove it; Corollary 5.10: RCA0^omega proves LINDbs <-> [QF-AC^{0,1}_R + LINDbsw]; Corollary 5.11: RCA0^omega proves [HBUbs + QF-AC^{0,1}_R] <-> [LINDbs + WKL].

statement.name: Weak Borel-Schoenflies Lindelof lemma
statement.definition: For every open covering of R provided by Psi : C -> Q^2 there is a sequence of intervals (a_n,b_n) covering R with each (a_n,b_n) equal to some J^Psi_x.
statement.facts: Theorem 5.7: Z_2^Omega proves it (and HBUbs); Corollary 5.8: RCA0^omega + (kappa^3_0) proves it.

statement.name: Borel-Schoenflies Heine-Borel theorem
statement.definition: For every open covering of [0,1] provided by Psi : C -> Q^2 there is a finite sub-covering.
statement.facts: Theorem 5.7: Z_2^Omega proves it; Corollary 5.11 (see LINDbs).

statement.name: Sequential Lindelof lemma for Baire space
statement.definition: (forall Psi_(.)^{0->2})(exists f_(.,.))(forall m)(forall g^1)(exists n)(g in [f_{n,m} Psi_m(f_{n,m})]).
statement.facts: Theorem 5.12: ACA0^omega + LINDseq proves Pi^1_1-CA0; equivalent to LIND(N^N) since N x N^N is homeomorphic to N^N.

statement.name: Uniform weak Konig's lemma
statement.definition: (forall G^2)(exists m)(forall T <=_1 1)[(forall alpha in C)(alpha G(alpha) not in T) -> (forall beta in C)(beta m not in T)].
statement.facts: Stated to be 'fairly easy' equivalent to HBU by adapting the proof of Corollary 4.6 (no proof given). Not the catalogue's WKL! (unique paths).

statement.name: Existence of a special fan functional
statement.definition: (exists Theta^3)(forall G^2)(forall f^1 <=_1 1)(exists g in Theta(G))(f in [g G(g)]): a functional computing a finite sub-covering for the canonical covering of Cantor space.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.5: ACA0^omega + QF-AC^{2,1} proves HBUc <-> HBU <-> (exists Theta)SCF(Theta) <-> PITu <-> (exists M)PR(M); Corollary 4.14: RCA0^omega + FF + QF-AC^{2,1} proves HBUc <-> (exists Theta)SCF(Theta).

statement.name: Existence of a Pincherle realiser
statement.definition: (exists M^3)(forall F,G : C -> N)[LOC(F,G) -> (forall g in C)(F(g) <= M(G))].
statement.facts: Theorem 4.5: equivalent to PITu over ACA0^omega + QF-AC^{2,1}. Theorems 3.1, 3.2: no PR is computable in a type two functional; Theorem 3.14: no weak Pincherle realiser either. Computability results, not catalogued as reductions.

statement.name: Fan functional
statement.definition: (exists Phi^3)(forall Y^2 in cont)(forall f,g in C)(f Phi(Y) = g Phi(Y) -> Y(f)=Y(g)).
statement.facts: Corollary 4.14: RCA0^omega + FF + QF-AC^{2,1} proves HBUc <-> (exists Theta)SCF(Theta); the base is conservative over WKL0.

statement.name: Comprehension on Cantor space
statement.definition: (exists kappa_0^3 <=_3 1)(forall Y^2)[kappa_0(Y)=0 <-> (exists f in C)Y(f)=0].
statement.facts: (exists^3) <-> [(exists^2) + (kappa^3_0)] (cited from [67,88]); RCA0^omega + (kappa^3_0) proves LINDbsw (Corollary 5.8).

statement.name: Quantifier-free choice from numbers to reals
statement.definition: For all F : R -> N: (forall n)(exists x in R)(F(x,n)=0) -> (exists Y^{0->1})(forall n)(F(Y(n),n)=0).
statement.facts: Theorem 5.3: RCA0^omega + LINDbs proves it; Corollary 5.10: Z_2^Omega proves LINDbs <-> QF-AC^{0,1}_R; its consequence (epsilon-delta vs sequential continuity) is independent of ZF.

statement.name: HBU without extensionality of Psi
statement.definition: HBU generalised to any functional Psi^{1->1} such that Psi(f) is a positive real, without requiring (RE).
statement.facts: Remark 4.15: RCA0^omega proves HBU <-> HBU+.

statement.name: Comprehension functional on Cantor space
statement.facts: Theorem 3.1: over WKL0^ω + QF-AC^{2,0}, (κ^3_0) ↔ (Z^3) + FF; Theorem 3.3 and Theorem 3.6 (splittings with MUC, (∃^3), WKL); (∃^3) ↔ (κ^3_0) + (∃^2).

statement.name: Functional testing continuity on Baire space
statement.facts: Corollary 3.2: RCA0^ω proves (∃^3) ↔ (∃^2) + (Z^3); Theorem 3.1; Theorem 3.7: (Z^3) ↔ [(∃^3) ∨ ¬(∃^2)].

statement.name: Complete theory with a non-principal type and finitely many models up to isomorphism (contraposition of Belanger Theorem 2.28)
statement.definition: Contraposition of: there is a complete theory with a non-principal type and only finitely many models up to isomorphism; T_0 ↔ WKL0 + ¬ACA0.
statement.facts: Corollary 3.12: RCA0^ω proves T_0 ↔ [WKL0 + ¬ACA0] ↔ [HBU + ¬ACA0]; Corollary 3.13: WKL0 ↔ [ACA0 ∨ T_0], T_1 ↔ (T_0 ∨ Σ02-IND).

statement.name: Powers of continuous maps on compact metric spaces (Friedman-Simpson-Yu Theorem 4.5.2)
statement.definition: For all k and all compact metric spaces X and continuous F: X → X, F^k is a continuous function from X into X; equivalent over RCA0 to WKL ∨ Σ02-IND.
statement.facts: Corollary 3.10: T_1 ↔ [HBU ∨ Σ02-IND] ↔ [WKL ∨ Σ02-IND] ↔ [FF ∨ HBU ∨ Σ02-IND].

statement.notation: BCT (Baire category theorem, open sets given by characteristic functions)
statement.name: Third-order Baire category theorem for open dense sets given by characteristic functions
statement.definition: For a sequence of dense open sets of [0,1], each given by a characteristic function, the intersection is nonempty.
statement.facts: RCA0^omega proves BCT -> NIN (Theorem 3.4); remains valid for open sets with finitely many isolated points in the complement. No Baire realiser is computable in a type-two functional (Theorem 4.4).

statement.name: Countably-compact metric spaces on [0,1] are separable
statement.definition: A countably-compact metric space ([0,1],d) is separable; unrelated to the stable thin set theorem.
statement.facts: RCA0^omega proves STS -> NIN (Theorem 3.12); also with 'separable' replaced by total boundedness, Heine-Borel or Lindelof property for uncountable covers, Vitali covering property (Corollary 3.13).

statement.name: Harnack: countable subsets of [0,1] have measure zero
statement.definition: A countable set A of [0,1] (Definition 3.14) has measure zero.
statement.facts: cocode0 -> Harnack0 -> Lebesgue0 -> NIN over RCA0^omega + WKL (Theorem 3.19); Pohm -> Harnack0 over ACA0^omega; the restriction to RM-closed sets still implies NIN (Corollary 3.20); Harnack1 (strongly countable sets) satisfies cocode1 -> Harnack1 -> NBI.

statement.name: Pigeonhole principle for measure (Tao)
statement.definition: For a sequence of sets E_n in [0,1], if the union has positive measure then some E_n has positive measure (assuming (E^2)).
statement.facts: ACA0^omega proves Pohm -> Harnack0 (Theorem 3.19); the restriction to RM-closed sets implies NIN (Corollary 3.20).

statement.name: Lebesgue criterion for Riemann integrability for countable exceptional sets
statement.definition: A bounded function on [0,1] continuous outside a countable set is Riemann integrable.
statement.facts: Harnack0 -> Lebesgue0 -> NIN over RCA0^omega + WKL (Theorem 3.19); the restriction to RM-closed sets implies NIN (Corollary 3.20).

statement.name: Heine-Borel theorem for strongly countable coverings
statement.loc: Theorem 3.33 (HBC0 restricted to strongly countable sets, Definition 3.32)
statement.definition: HBC0 restricted to strongly countable sets A of R^2.
statement.facts: RCA0^omega proves HBC1 -> NBI (Theorem 3.33); [cocode1 + WKL] -> HBC1 over RCA0^omega (Corollary 3.36); Z^omega_2 + HBC1 cannot prove NIN.

statement.name: Bolzano-Weierstrass theorem for countable subsets of [0,1]
statement.definition: A countable set in [0,1] has a supremum.
statement.facts: BW0 -> HBC0 by the usual proof; Z^omega_2 + QF-AC^{0,1} cannot prove HBC0 or BW0 (Corollary 3.23); ACA0 -> BW1 given Delta-CA.

statement.name: NCC with only an upper bound
statement.definition: NCC where g only provides an upper bound on the m-variable.
statement.facts: RCA0^omega + NCC_w proves NBI (Corollary 3.31).

statement.name: Sigma neighbourhood function principle
statement.definition: For A(sigma) = (exists g in 2^N)(Y(g,sigma)=0): (forall f)(exists n)A(fn) -> (exists g in K_0)(forall f)A(f g(f)); fragment of NFP.
statement.facts: Implies NCC, and HBU together with WKL, as shown in [100, §5].

statement.name: BOOT^- restricted to Cantor space
statement.definition: For Y^2 with at most one f in 2^N such that Y(f,n)=0, the set {n : exists g in 2^N Y(g,n)=0} exists.
statement.facts: BW^C_0 -> BOOT^-_C; Pi^1_1-CA_0^omega + BOOT^-_C proves Pi^1_2-CA_0.

statement.name: Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem for countable sets in [0,1]
statement.definition: For countable A ⊂ [0,1] and F : [0,1] → [0,1], the supremum sup_{x∈A} F(x) exists.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.16: equivalent to cocode0, BOOT^-_C, CBN + cocode1 over RCA0^ω (and to MCT0^net over ACA0^ω); Cor. 3.17: with the Suslin functional it yields Π12-CA0; Cor. 3.18: not provable in Z2^ω + QF-AC^{0,1}, adds no L2-sentence beyond RCA0. Close to catalogue bwc0fun (Cantor space version, equivalent given (∃2)).

statement.name: Monotone convergence theorem for nets with countable index sets
statement.definition: Every increasing net in [0,1] indexed by finite sequences without repetitions of a countable set A (ordered by inclusion) converges.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.16 (over ACA0^ω): equivalent to BW_0^{[0,1]}, BOOT^-_C, cocode0, CBN + cocode1; Theorem 3.21: MCT_0^net ↔ [MCT_1^net + CBN] over ACA0^ω.

statement.name: Bootstrap principle with unique witnesses on Cantor space
statement.definition: BOOT^- with N^N replaced by 2^N: for Y with at most one f ∈ 2^N with Y(f,n)=0 for each n, {n : ∃f Y(f,n)=0} exists.
statement.facts: Equivalent to cocode0 and BW_0^{[0,1]} (Theorem 3.16); BOOT^-_C → cocode0 from [64, Thm 3.16].

statement.name: Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem for strongly countable sets
statement.definition: For a strongly countable set A ⊂ [0,1] there is a sequence in A converging to the supremum of A.
statement.facts: Corollary 3.22: over RCA0^ω + IND_Σ, BW_1^{[0,1]} ↔ cocode1; not explosive.

statement.name: Monotone convergence theorem for nets with strongly countable index sets with modulus of convergence
statement.definition: MCT_0^net restricted to strongly countable index sets and upgraded with a modulus of convergence.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.21: over ACA0^ω, MCT_1^net ↔ cocode1 ↔ !QF-AC^{0,1}.

statement.name: Quantifier-free choice with unique existence
statement.definition: QF-AC^{0,1} restricted to unique existence.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.21: equivalent to cocode1 and MCT_1^net over ACA0^ω.

statement.name: Naive Cantor–Bernstein theorem
statement.definition: CBN with condition (ii) replaced by: there is an injection from N to A.
statement.facts: Corollary 3.23: over RCA0^ω + NCC, cocode0 ↔ CBN' ↔ [CBN' + fin0]; with Korg0 and ADS0 splittings (Cor. 3.33, 3.44).

statement.name: Finite sets can be listed by sequences
statement.definition: cocode0 restricted: for A ⊂ [0,1] and Y injective and bounded on A, there is a sequence listing A.
statement.facts: Used in Corollaries 3.23, 3.33, 3.44: cocode0 ↔ [CBN' + fin0] over RCA0^ω + NCC.

statement.name: Induction for Σ-formulas
statement.definition: Induction axiom for formulas ϕ(n) ≡ (∃f ∈ N^N)(Z(f,n) = 0).
statement.facts: Extra base axiom in Corollary 3.22 and Theorem 3.42.

statement.name: König's infinity lemma for graphs/sets with countable vertex sets
statement.definition: Korg0: for a graph with countable vertex set V = ∪Vn, each Vn non-empty finite and each vertex of Vn+1 adjacent to one of Vn, there is a path (vn) with vn ∈ Vn; Korg1: restricted to strongly countable V; Korg2: the set version with a binary relation on reals.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.32: Korg1 → NBI over RCA0^ω; Cor. 3.33: Korg1 ↔ cocode1, cocode0 ↔ [Korg0 + CBN]; Cor. 3.34: Δ-CA proves Korg1, RCA0^ω + Korg1 does not prove ACA0; Theorem 3.36: Korg2 → cocode1, and RCA0^ω + ACA0^ω + Π12-IND + QF-AC^{0,1} proves Korg2.

statement.name: ADS for countable (strongly countable) linear orders of reals
statement.definition: ADS_0: every countable infinite linear order has an infinite ascending or descending sequence; ADS_1 for strongly countable; SADS_0 for stable orders.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.42: over RCA0^ω + IND_Σ, ADS_0 → NBI; Cor. 3.43: ADS_0 → cocode1, ADS_0 does not imply ADS; Cor. 3.44: cocode0 ↔ [ADS_0 + CBN] over RCA0^ω + IND_Σ; Cor. 3.45 for SADS_0; Cor. 3.46 under MUC. Similar remarks for CAC and RT^2_2 (Section 3.5).

statement.name: Monotone nets indexed by N^N have monotone subnets with countable index set
statement.definition: A monotone net in [0,1] indexed by N^N has a monotone sub-net with a countable index set.
statement.facts: Corollary 3.27: over ACA0^ω, [BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1}] ↔ [BOOT^-_C + SUBNET_0].

statement.name: Third-order countability statements equivalent to (∃2)
statement.definition: Any sequence of reals is a countable set; the unit interval is first-countable; (∃Y^2)(∀f,g ∈ N∞)(Y(f)=Y(g) → f=g) (with surjectivity); the unit interval second-countable.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.5: over RCA0^ω each of the first four is equivalent to (∃2); (∃2) follows from second-countability; Cor. 3.6: (ii) → (i) over RCA0^ω + WKL.

statement.name: HBC for RM-codes
statement.definition: HBC with C ⊆ [0,1] represented by RM-codes; equivalent to WKL ([3, Lemma 3.13]).
statement.facts: Used in the proof of Theorem 3.6.

statement.name: Pincherle's theorem with weakened antecedent
statement.definition: PIT_o with LOC(F,G) replaced by (∀f∈C)(∃n)(∀g∈C)(g∈[f n] → F(g) ≤ n).
statement.facts: Corollary 3.3: RCA0^omega + NCC proves WKL <-> PIT'_o.

statement.name: Urysohn lemma for closed sets in the sense of Definition 3.4
statement.definition: For closed disjoint C0, C1 ⊆ R there is a continuous g: R→[0,1] with x∈Ci ↔ g(x)=i.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.11: RCA0^omega + NCC + coco proves TIE <-> URY (URY -> TIE over RCA0^omega, cited from [30, §5]).

statement.name: Tietze extension theorem (Definition 3.10, sets as in Definition 3.4)
statement.definition: For f: R→R continuous on the closed D ⊂ [0,1] there is g continuous on [0,1] with f=g on D. Differs from catalogue tietze (moduli of uniform continuity).
statement.facts: See URY.

statement.name: Every continuous Y: R→R has an RM-code
statement.definition: Every continuous function R→R has an RM-code (as in [18, §4]); its ECF-interpretation is a tautology.
statement.facts: Used as extra hypothesis in Theorem 3.11.

statement.name: Coding principle open+
statement.definition: For every open set Z ⊆ R (Definition 3.12) there is X ⊆ N with n∈X ↔ B(q_n,r_n) ⊆ Z.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.14: RCA0^omega + NCC proves BOOT <-> [open+ + ACA0]. Cited [40, §4.2]: BOOT + ACA0 <-> open+ using QF-AC^{0,1}.

statement.name: Cantor-Bendixson theorem for closed sets of [0,1] (third-order)
statement.definition: Any closed set C ⊆ [0,1] is P ∪ S with P perfect closed and S a sequence of reals. Differs from catalogue cb (second-order).
statement.facts: Cited [40, §4]: [ACA0 + CBT] <-> [Pi11-CA0 + BOOT] over RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}; the paper says it holds with NCC instead (not proved).

statement.name: Universal-quantifier version of NCC
statement.facts: Used for the Baire category theorem; realisers: Corollary 4.7, RCA0^omega proves (∃ϑ)MCC(ϑ) <-> (∃^3).

statement.name: Existence of a total realiser for NCC
statement.definition: There is a functional ζ^{2→1} with NCC(ζ): (∀n)(∃m)A(n,m) → (∀n)A(n,ζ(Y)(n)).
statement.facts: Theorem 4.5: RCA0^omega proves (∃ζ)NCC(ζ) <-> (∃^3). Lemmas 4.3, 4.4: it implies (κ^3_0) and (∃^2).

statement.name: Existence of a weak total realiser for NCC
statement.definition: ζw with (∀n)(∃m)A(n,m) → (∀n)(∃m ≤ ζw(n))A(n,m).
statement.facts: Theorem 4.11: RCA0^omega proves (∃ζw)NCCw(ζw) <-> (∃^3) (Lemmas 4.9, 4.10).

statement.name: Comprehension on Cantor space
Existence of a countably based partial realiser for NCC
statement.definition: Partial functional ζp with ζp(Y) a choice function whenever the hypothesis of NCC holds, countably based as in Definition 2.6.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.19: over ZFC equivalent to the Continuum Hypothesis; no partial NCC-realiser is computable in a type 2 functional (Corollary 4.16).

statement.name: Generalizations of weak König's lemma to Φn-/Ψn-trees
statement.definition: WKL for trees given by formulas ∀f1≤1 s1 ∃f2≤1 s2 … ∀x A0 (Φn) or starting with ∃ (Ψn), with bounded function quantifiers and arbitrary-type parameters; Φ∞-WKL is the union over n.
statement.facts: Proposition 5.7: over E-Gk A^ω (k≥3), E-PRA^ω or E-PA^ω, WKL, Φ0-WKL, Ψ0-WKL and Φ_m^-/Ψ_n^- -WKL (parameters of type ≤1) are all equivalent. Proposition 5.11: E-PA^ω + Φ_{n+1}-WKL proves Π^{1,b}_n-CA. Proposition 5.13: E-PA^ω+QF-AC^{1,0}+QF-AC^{0,1}+µ does not prove Φ1-WKL (so with µ the hierarchy is non-collapsing; Φn-WKL, Ψn-WKL underivable for n≥2).

statement.name: Uniform strengthenings of Φn-WKL
statement.definition: ∀h ∃a ∃f≤1 1 ∀ñ≤h(a) A(a,fñ) → ∃a ∃f≤1 1 ∀n A(a,fn), for A in Φn (resp. Ψn).
statement.facts: Proposition 5.17: Φ0-WKL ↔ Φ0-WKL+ over T+QF-AC^{0,0}. Proposition 6.1: T+QF-AC^{1,0}+F^- proves Φ∞-WKL+. Theorem 7.2: E-PRA^ω+QF-AC^{1,0}+QF-AC^{0,1}+Φ∞-WKL+ is Π^0_2-conservative over PRA (E-PA^ω version conservative over PA). Ψ1-WKL+ suffices for a modulus of uniform continuity of continuous functionals on {f≤1}.

statement.name: Uniform Σ⁰₁-boundedness
statement.definition: ∀y^{1(0)}(∀k∀x≤1 yk ∃z A(x,y,k,z) → ∃χ ∀k ∀x≤1 yk ∃z≤χk A(x,y,k,z)) for A Σ⁰₁ with arbitrary-type parameters; non-standard (false in the full set-theoretic model).
statement.facts: Proposition 3.2: T+QF-AC^{1,0}+F proves it; Proposition 3.3: E-G3A^ω+Σ01-UB proves WKL; Theorem 7.1: T+QF-AC^{1,0}+QF-AC^{0,1}+Σ01-UB is Π^0_2-conservative over EA/PRA and conservative over PA; it implies Φ∞-WKL+.

statement.name: Exact numerical choice with higher-order parameters
statement.definition: ENC with type-2 (higher-order) parameters allowed in the Π-formula φ.
statement.facts: ACA0^ω + ENC^ω proves ATR0 (Theorem 2.5(b)); over ACA0^ω+Σ-IND, ENC^ω ↔ [BNC^ω + Φ1-KL] (Theorem 3.9) and ↔ [BNC^ω + Φ1-WKL] ↔ [BNC^ω + HBT]; with open†, implies open (Theorem 3.15).

statement.name: Bounding numerical choice with higher-order parameters
statement.definition: BNC with higher-order parameters allowed in the Π-formula φ.
statement.facts: Over ACA0^ω+QF-AC^{0,1}, equivalent to: sub-continuous / everywhere Riemann integrable f:R→R is dominated by a continuous function, existence of a modulus of Riemann integration, etc. (Theorem 2.7); over ACA0^ω+QF-AC^{0,1}+Σ-IND equivalent to boundedness properties of sequentially compact metric spaces, Dini, uniform size bounds of cuf sets (Theorem 2.13); ACA0^ω + BNC proves NIN[0,1] (Theorem 2.5(d)).

statement.name: Riemann integrable functions on R are dominated by a continuous function
statement.definition: For f:R→R Riemann integrable on every [-a,a], there is continuous g:R→R with f(x) ≤ g(x) for all x.
statement.facts: Equivalent to BNC^ω over ACA0^ω+QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem 2.7(c)); implies ATR0 (Theorem 2.3(e)).

statement.name: Kohlenbach's weak lemma (WKL for Π-formula trees)
statement.definition: For A(σ) of the form (∀g∈2^N)B(g,σ), B arithmetical: (∀n)(∃f∈2^N)(∀m≤n)A(f m) → (∃f∈2^N)(∀n)A(f n).
statement.facts: Over ACA0^ω+Σ-IND: HBT ↔ Φ1-WKL ↔ [HBU + A0] (Theorem 3.6); not provable in Z2^ω+QF-AC^{0,1} (Corollary 3.7); implies cocode0-type enumeration of countable sets of reals; ENC^ω_b ↔ Φ1-WKL.

statement.name: Kohlenbach's lemma (finitely branching version)
statement.definition: Φ1-WKL for finitely branching Π-class trees over N^N.
statement.facts: ENC^ω ↔ [BNC^ω + Φ1-KL] over ACA0^ω+Σ-IND (Theorem 3.9); equivalent to Ramsey's theorem for Π-classes (Remark 3.12).

statement.name: Kohlenbach's Ψ1-WKL (Σ-formula trees)
statement.definition: Φ1-WKL with ∀g replaced by ∃g.
statement.facts: Provable in ACA0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem 3.11).

statement.name: Induction for Σ-formulas
statement.definition: Induction axiom for formulas (∃f∈N^N)(Y(f,n)=0) with Y of type 2.
statement.facts: Used as extra hypothesis in Theorems 1.9, 2.13, 2.15, 3.3, 3.6, 3.9.

statement.name: Open sets of reals are RM-open (coding principle)
statement.definition: Every open set O ⊂ R is RM-open (union of countably many open intervals).
statement.facts: Equivalent to item (c) of Theorem 3.15 over ACA0^ω+QF-AC^{0,1}; ENC^ω + open† implies open; open + open† relates to Lindelöf and OC0,0 (Theorem 3.18).

statement.name: Open sets of reals are Fσ
statement.definition: An open set O ⊂ R is Fσ: O = ∪ C_n for increasing closed C_n.
statement.facts: Does not imply NIN[0,1]; BNC^ω + open† implies BCT[0,1] over ACA0^ω (Corollary 3.16).

statement.name: R2-open sets are RM-open
statement.definition: An R2-open set O ⊂ R is RM-open.
statement.facts: Part of Theorem 3.15 (b),(c); follows from HBU.

statement.name: Open choice
statement.definition: For increasing open sets (On) of R with (∀n)(∃m)([-n,n]⊂Om), there is g with (∀n)([-n,n]⊂O_g(n)).
statement.facts: Follows from BNC^ω; Theorem 3.18(c): Lindelöf + OC0,0 ↔ open over ACA0^ω+QF-AC^{0,1}.

statement.name: Baire category theorem for the unit interval (third-order)
statement.definition: For a decreasing sequence of dense open sets in [0,1], the intersection is non-empty.
statement.facts: BNC^ω + open† implies BCT[0,1] over ACA0^ω (Corollary 3.16).

statement.name: Tao's pigeon hole principle for measure
statement.definition: For a sequence of closed sets of reals of measure zero, the union has measure zero.
statement.facts: Implied by ENC^ω (Remark 2.9); shown in Figure 1.

statement.name: Anti-Specker property for nets with a bounded-away modulus
statement.definition: AS_net where the antecedent supplies F : R -> R giving the bound delta at each x.
statement.facts: RCA_0^omega + IND proves HBU <-> AS^-_net (Theorem 3.15).

statement.name: Cauchy nets in [0,1] converge
statement.definition: A Cauchy net in [0,1] converges to a limit.
statement.facts: RCA_0^omega + IND + CAU_net proves HBU (Theorem 3.20); a realiser for CAU_net together with exists2 computes exists3 and vice versa (Corollary 3.22).

statement.name: Increasing nets in [0,1] are Cauchy
statement.definition: An increasing net in [0,1] is a Cauchy net.
statement.facts: RCA_0^omega + IND proves CAU'_net; a realiser for it together with exists2 computes exists3 (Corollary 3.21).

statement.name: Cauchy sub-nets
statement.definition: Any net in the unit interval contains a Cauchy sub-net.
statement.facts: A realiser for COH_net computes exists3 (by Corollary 3.21); needed to derive BW_net from CAU_net.

statement.name: Monotone sub-nets
statement.definition: A net in R has a monotone sub-net.
statement.facts: BW_net is said to imply MCT_net but the reversal seems to need ADS_net; conjectured not to follow from MCT_net; [(exists3) + QF-AC^{1,1}] -> ADS_net.

statement.name: Neighbourhood function principle without codes
statement.definition: For any Pi^1_infinity formula A with a type-two parameter: (forall f)(exists n) A(fn) -> (exists Phi^2)(forall f) A(f Phi(f)).
statement.facts: RCA_0^omega + IND + NFP_0 + HBU proves MCT^0_net (Theorem 3.5), so HBU <-> MCT^0_net over RCA_0^omega + IND + NFP_0 (Corollary 3.6). Differs from the catalogue's nfp3 (associates).

statement.name: Unordered sums (permutation theorem)
statement.definition: For D subset of Baire space and a_d : D -> R, if the net of finite partial sums is Cauchy it converges.
statement.facts: A realiser for PERM computes exists2 and a realiser for ATR_0 (Theorem 3.24).

statement.name: Sequentialisation of nets of functions
statement.definition: For an increasing net of continuous functions f_d converging to continuous f, there is Phi : N -> D with f_Phi(n) increasing and converging to f.
statement.facts: RCA_0^omega + SUB proves LIN (Theorem 4.3), where LIN is the catalogue's lind.

statement.name: Sequentialisation of increasing nets in [0,1]
statement.definition: For an increasing net x_d in I converging to x, there is Phi : N -> D with x_Phi(n) increasing and converging to x.
statement.facts: RCA_0^omega + IND proves SUB_0 -> QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem 4.5); RCA_0^omega + IND + ADS proves SUB_0 <-> QF-AC^{0,1} (Corollary 4.6).

statement.name: ADS for uncountable linear orders
statement.definition: For an infinite linear order (D, <=_D) with D subset of Baire space there is an ascending or descending sequence.
statement.facts: RCA_0^omega + IND + ADS_2 proves QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem 4.8); ZF cannot prove ADS_2 (Corollary 4.9).

statement.name: Net-continuity equals epsilon-delta continuity (local)
statement.definition: f : R -> R is net-continuous at x if f(x_d) converges to f(x) for every net x_d converging to x.
statement.facts: RCA_0^omega proves net-continuity at x <-> epsilon-delta continuity at x (Theorem 4.11), without choice; ZF cannot prove the local equivalence of net-continuity and sequential continuity (Corollary 4.12).

statement.name: Net-closed sets in R are closed; R is a sequential space
statement.definition: A set F is net-closed if limits of nets in F lie in F; sequentially closed likewise with sequences.
statement.facts: RCA_0^omega proves every net-closed set in R is closed (Theorem 4.15); RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} proves R is a sequential space (Theorem 4.14).

statement.name: Sub-continuous functions are locally bounded
statement.definition: f : R -> R is sub-continuous if f(x_d) has a convergent sub-net whenever x_d converges to x.
statement.facts: RCA_0^omega proves sub-continuous functions are locally bounded (Theorem 4.17).

statement.name: Monotone convergence for nets indexed by subsets of N^N -> N
statement.definition: Any increasing net x_e : E -> [0,1] indexed by a subset E of (N^N -> N) converges.
statement.facts: A realiser for MCT^1_net computes exists4 and vice versa (Theorem A.3).

statement.name: Monotone convergence for nets defined arithmetically
statement.definition: MCT^0_net restricted to directed sets and nets defined by arithmetical formulas.
statement.facts: A realiser computes S^2 via a term of Goedel's T and vice versa (Theorem A.4); with type-two parameters it computes the superjump S^3 (Corollary A.5).

statement.name: Sequentialisation for nets indexed by subsets of N^N -> N
statement.definition: As SUB_0 for increasing nets x_e : E -> I with E subset of (N^N -> N).
statement.facts: ACA_0^omega + IND proves SUB_1 -> QF-AC^{0,2} (Theorem A.7); ACA_0^omega + IND + ADS proves SUB_1 <-> QF-AC^{0,2} (Corollary A.8).

statement.name: Uniform intermediate value theorem / uniform Weierstrass maximum theorem
statement.definition: UIVT: there is a functional Phi^{(1->1)->1} with f(Phi(f))=0 for every continuous f on [0,1] with f(0)>=0, f(1)<=0. UWEIMAX: a functional giving a maximiser of every continuous f on [0,1].
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to (exists2) (Kohlenbach [36, Prop. 3.14]; Corollary 3.11, Theorem 3.13), over RCA0^Omega with nonstandard equivalents.

statement.name: Uniform fan theorems
statement.definition: UFAN_1: functional Phi^2 bounding the height of every binary tree without path. UFAN_2: functional Phi(T,g) bounding the height of a binary tree T for which g witnesses that T has no path.
statement.facts: UFAN_1 is equivalent to (exists2) relative to st (Theorem 5.3); UFAN_2 relative to st is equivalent to FAN^st; over RCA0^omega+QF-AC^{2,0}, FAN <-> UFAN_2 (Corollary 5.5, the paper states it over RCA0^Omega).

statement.name: Uniform Heine-Borel lemma, supremum and Riemann integral functionals
statement.definition: Functionals giving a finite subcover bound (given a witness g), the supremum, resp. the integral of a continuous function.
statement.facts: Equivalent to FAN^st (and over QF-AC^{2,0} to the fan theorem) in RCA0^Omega: Corollaries 5.7, 5.13, 5.14.

statement.name: Fan functional restricted to continuous functionals
statement.definition: Existence of a modulus of uniform continuity functional for type-2 functionals continuous in a given sense on Cantor space.
statement.facts: Over RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{2,0}, FAN <-> MUC(CC) (Theorem 5.8); relative to st, FAN^st <-> MUC(Crm)^st (Theorem 5.11).

statement.name: Functional form of ATR0 and its uniform version
statement.definition: ATR_o: for all f,X, WO(X) implies exists Y H_f(X,Y) with theta(n,Y) = forall k f(k,n,Yk)=0 (Pi01 form, unlike the catalogue uatr which is Sigma01 and omits no parameter). UATR_o: a functional Phi(f,X) giving Y.
statement.facts: Corollary 6.2: over RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{1,1}, [ATR_o + (exists2)] <-> UATR_o. Not entered because UATR_o differs in form from the catalogue uatr (Pi vs Sigma).

statement.name: Uniform perfect set theorem
statement.definition: UPST_1: a functional Phi(T) giving a nonempty perfect subtree of any tree with uncountably many paths. UPST_2: Phi(T,g) where g witnesses the uncountability.
statement.facts: Theorem 6.5: over RCA0^omega, UPST_1 <-> (S^2) (cited from Normann-Sanders-type result [46, Theorem 4.4]); over RCA0^omega + (exists2) + QF-AC^{1,1}, UPST_2 <-> ATR_o.

statement.notation: Pi01-TRANS, Pi11-TRANS, WKL*, FAN*, Omega-CA, STP
statement.name: Nonstandard transfer and standard-part principles
statement.definition: Nelson-style nonstandard principles over RCA0^Omega (language with standardness predicate st).
statement.facts: Pi01-TRANS <-> (exists2) <-> WKL* in RCA0^Omega (Theorem 3.1, Theorem 2.3); Pi11-TRANS <-> (S^2) ([5, Cor. 14]). Not expressible in the catalogue (nonstandard framework).

statement.name: Topological (covering) dimension statements
statement.definition: Every open cover (generated by psi: I -> R) has a refinement of order at most m+1, for the unit interval with m=1; dim(R)<=1 likewise for R.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.5: ACA0^omega + QF-AC^{1,1} + [dim([0,1])<=1] proves HBT. Corollary 3.6: over RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{1,1}, WKL + [dim(I)=1] <-> HBT. Corollary 3.18: over RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{1,1}, LIL <-> [dim(R)<=1] <-> R is paracompact. Corollary 3.20 over RCA0^omega + IND + (kappa_0^3): [dim(R)<=1] + QF-AC^{0,1} <-> [R paracompact] + QF-AC^{0,1} <-> LIL.

statement.name: Urysohn identity dim X = ind X = Ind X for the unit interval
statement.definition: The topological dimension, small and large inductive dimension of [0,1] coincide.
statement.facts: Corollary 3.8: over RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{1,1}, HBT <-> WKL + Urysohn identity for the unit interval.

statement.name: Paracompactness of the unit interval (higher-order)
statement.definition: Every open cover (generated by psi: I -> R) has a locally finite open refinement covering [0,1]; similarly for R.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.11: ACA0^omega + QF-AC^{1,1} + [0,1] paracompact proves HBT. Corollary 3.12: over RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{1,1}, WKL + [0,1] paracompact <-> HBT. Corollary 3.18 for R (see above). Remark 3.13: not provable in the union of Pi^1_k-CA0^omega. Theorem 3.24: effective paracompactness of R.

statement.name: Lindelof lemma, strong version for covers psi: R -> R^2
statement.definition: For every psi: R -> R^2 with R contained in the union of the intervals J_x^psi (possibly empty), there is f: N -> R with R contained in the union of J^psi_{f(n)}.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.17: over RCA0^omega + QF-AC^{1,1}, LIN <-> LIL; HBT <-> WKL + LIL over the same base. Theorem 3.19: over RCA0^omega + (kappa_0^3) + IND, [LIN + QF-AC^{0,1}] <-> LIL.

statement.name: Existence of partitions of unity dominated by covers
statement.definition: For any cover generated by psi: I -> R (resp. psi: R -> R^2) there is a partition of unity dominated by it.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.22: over RCA0^omega + (kappa_0^3) + IND, [WKL + PUNI(I)] <-> HBT. Theorem 3.24: [PUNI(R) + QF-AC^{0,1}] <-> LIL <-> [R effectively paracompact + QF-AC^{0,1}] over the same base.

statement.name: Comprehension for Cantor space functional; C-formula neighbourhood function principle; full induction
statement.definition: (kappa_0^3): kappa(Y)=0 iff (exists f in C)(Y(f)>0). C-NFP_0: for C-formulas A, (forall f)(exists n)A(fn) -> (exists Phi^2)(forall f)A(f Phi(f)). IND: induction for all formulas of L_omega.
statement.facts: Used as base theory extras: HBU <-> HBT over RCA0^omega + IND + (kappa_0^3) (Theorem 3.16) and over RCA0^omega + IND + C-NFP_0 (Corollary 3.27). C-NFP_0 is a generalisation of the catalogued A_0 (formulas are Boolean combinations of basic C-formulas), not the same statement.

statement.name: Transfer for Π01-formulas
statement.definition: (∀st f)[(∀st n)(f(n) ≠ 0) → (∀m)(f(m) ≠ 0)]; nonstandard counterpart of ACA0 (term extraction gives Feferman's µ2).
statement.facts: P + Π01-TRANS does not prove STP (Theorem 4.5) nor ATR0 relative to st (Theorem 6.2); proves Δ11-CA relative to st (Theorem 6.1).

statement.name: Transfer for Π11-formulas
statement.definition: Standard-parameter transfer for Π11 formulas; nonstandard counterpart of Π11-CA0 (term extraction gives the Suslin functional / µ1).
statement.facts: P + Π11-TRANS does not prove STP (Corollary 4.6) nor LMP (Theorem 4.10).

statement.name: Nonstandard uniform continuity on Cantor space
statement.definition: Every standard type-2 functional is nonstandard uniformly continuous on Cantor space.
statement.facts: P + NUC proves STP and WT (Theorem 6.14); gives the intuitionistic fan functional by term extraction.

statement.name: Weak Transfer for type-2 functionals, and Transfer for type-2 and type-3 existential statements
statement.definition: SOT/TOT: (∀st Y)((∃f)(Y(f)=0) → (∃st f)(Y(f)=0)) etc.; WT is the version restricted to f ≤ 1.
statement.facts: P + X + TOT proves STP (Theorem 4.7); P + NUC proves STP and WT.

statement.name: Functional κ (higher-order version of Kohlenbach's Π1,b_n-CA)
statement.facts: Computable from the intuitionistic fan functional by a term of Gödel's T (Remark 6.13, Corollary 6.15); RCA0^ω + WKL + (κ) is conservative over RCA0^2 + WKL; any κ computes a special fan functional but no κ is computable in a Θ (Theorem 6.17); κ with ∃2 computes ∃3.

statement.name: Classical fan functional
statement.definition: Φ gives a modulus of uniform continuity on Cantor space for every continuous Y (Y ∈ C).
statement.facts: Computable in ∃2 (Kohlenbach); the special fan functional restricted to Y ∈ C is computable from it.

statement.name: Effective fan theorem
statement.facts: Implied by SFF(Θ) via a term (Theorem 3.4); implies FAN in RCA0^ω.

statement.name: Uniform (effective) monotone convergence theorem
statement.loc: Section 4.1.1, (4.1) and Theorem 4.1; Corollary 4.3 for MCT'_ef
statement.definition: There is a functional t of type 0->1 to ... such that for every increasing sequence c of reals bounded by 1 and every k, |c_M - c_N| <= 1/k for all M, N >= t(c)(k) (a rate of convergence functional); MCT'_ef also outputs the limit.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.1 and Corollary 4.3: over RCA_0^omega, (mu^2) implies MCT_ef(s(mu)) and MCT_ef(t) implies MU(u(t)), an explicit equivalence with (mu^2) (and (exists^2)); the Herbrandisation MCT_her is discussed in Section 4.1.2.

statement.name: Uniform intermediate value theorem
statement.definition: A functional t with: for f with modulus of continuity g and f(0)>0, f(1)<0, f(t(g,f)) =_R 0.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.24: explicit equivalence with (mu^2) over RCA_0^omega (attributed to Kohlenbach [45, Section 3] for (exists t)IVT_ef(t) <-> (exists^2)); the weak version IVT'_ef (approximate zeros) is provable in E-PRA^omega* (Theorem 4.24 second part) and constructively (Corollary 4.25). Analogous results are claimed for the Weierstrass maximum theorem (WEIMAX_ef, Theorem 4.27) without proof.

statement.name: Uniform torsion subgroup theorem
statement.definition: A functional t returning, for each countable abelian group G, a torsion subgroup T together with a functional h with h(g)g = 0 for g in T; TOR is 'a countable abelian group has a subgroup consisting of the torsion elements'.
statement.facts: Corollary 4.49: (mu^2) <-> (exists t)TOR_ef(t) is an explicit equivalence provable in RCA_0^omega. The paper also refers to TOR <-> ACA_0 in [83, III.6.2], and obtains (4.64) via standard extensionality (Corollary 4.50).

statement.name: Feferman's version of the Suslin functional
statement.definition: A functional mu^1 of type 1->1 such that for every f^1, if (exists g)(forall x) f(gx) != 0 then (forall x) f(mu^1(f) x) != 0.
statement.facts: Corollary 4.45: in RCA_0^omega, (mu^1) <-> (exists t)PST_ef(t) explicitly (PST: every tree with uncountably many paths has a non-empty perfect subtree); Corollary 4.46: (forall t) DIV_ef(t) -> MUO(u(t)) (DIV: divisible/reduced decomposition). Probably equivalent to the Suslin functional (S^2) but the paper does not state this.

statement.name: Effective Heine-Borel, fan theorem, Heine's theorem and Dini's theorem
statement.definition: Effective versions of the Heine-Borel covering lemma for [0,1] (HBL_ef(h)), of the fan theorem (the contraposition of WKL, FAN_ef(h)), of Heine's theorem (continuous implies uniformly continuous on [0,1], HEI_ef(t)) and of Dini's theorem (DINI_ef(t)), with a functional bounding the finite subcover or modulus.
statement.facts: Corollaries 4.20, 4.21 and Theorems 4.19, 4.30: the effective versions are explicitly equivalent over E-PRA^omega* (in RCA_0^omega); the paper says the non-effective equivalence of Heine-Borel, the fan theorem and Heine's theorem is well known (Simpson [83, IV.2.3]) and cites [7, Section 5] for Dini's theorem equivalent to WKL_0. Corollary 4.35: the Herbrandised form (exists Theta)HEI_her(Theta) is equivalent to the special fan functional.

statement.name: Standard Part for Cantor space and fragments of Transfer (nonstandard principles)
statement.definition: Principles of Nelson-style nonstandard analysis: STP says every binary sequence is infinitely close to a standard one; Pi^0_1-TRANS and Pi^1_1-TRANS are Transfer restricted to those formula classes.
statement.facts: Theorems 4.1, 4.16, 4.24, 4.44: MCT_ns, IVT_ns and TOR_ns are equivalent to Pi^0_1-TRANS, PST_ns to Pi^1_1-TRANS, and HBL_ns, HEI_ns, DINI_ns to STP over P_0 (a fragment of internal set theory); the Herbrandisations are (mu^2), (mu^1) and the existence of a special fan functional respectively. These principles are not statements of the zoo.

statement.name: Boundedness of metastable sequences
statement.definition: If for all sequences x the metastability condition (forall k, g)(exists N <= h(k,g)) A(k,g,N,x) implies |x_n| <= Phi(h), then Phi is a functional providing upper bounds for metastable sequences.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.6: a term t computes the Turing jump (MU(t(Phi))) from any such functional Phi, so even upper bounds for metastable sequences have non-computable content.

statement.name: Heine–Borel theorem for uncountable canonical coverings of closed sets
statement.definition: HBU generalised to closed sets C ⊆ [0,1] in the sense of Definition 1.2.
statement.facts: Has the first-order strength of WKL; Z_2^Ω proves it (as in [37, Theorem 4.2]); RCA0^ω + HBU_closed proves HBC (Theorem 3.3); RCA0^ω proves (∃³) → HBU_closed → HBC (Section 1.2(c)); RCA0^ω + IND^ω proves NFP → BOOT → HBU_closed (Theorem 4.5).

statement.name: Strong countable Heine–Borel theorem for coverings by arbitrary open sets
statement.definition: For closed C ⊆ [0,1] and a sequence of open sets (O_n) (Definition 1.2) with C ⊆ ∪O_n, some finite subfamily covers C.
statement.facts: Z_2^ω does not prove it (Theorem 3.15); RCA0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} proves WKL ↔ HBC_s (Theorem 3.16).

statement.name: Weak Heine–Borel theorem for countable coverings of closed sets
statement.definition: For ε>0, closed C ⊆ [0,1] and a covering by (a_n,b_n), there are finitely many (a_n,b_n) and further intervals (c_m,d_m) of total length < ε covering C.
statement.facts: Z_2^ω does not prove WHBC (Theorem 3.12); WWKL ↔ WHBC provable as in Corollary 3.4 with the coding principle that continuous functionals on Baire space have codes (stated without full proof).

statement.name: Every open set (third-order characteristic function) has an RM-code
statement.definition: For every open set Y ⊆ R (Definition 1.2) there is X ⊆ N with (∀n)(n ∈ X ↔ B(q_n,r_n) ⊆ Y).
statement.facts: Z_2^Ω proves open, Z_2^ω does not, Π¹_k-CA0^ω does not prove it (Section 1.2, Theorem 4.17); RCA0^ω proves BOOT → [open + ACA0] → BOOT^- (Theorem 4.5); Π¹_k-CA0^ω + open implies Π¹_k-TR0 (Corollary 4.6); CLO ↔ [ACA0 + open] (Theorem 4.12); ACA0^ω proves URY ↔ open (Theorem 5.3), RCA0^ω + coco proves URY ↔ open (Corollary 5.4); no type-two functional computes a Ψ-functional, ∃³ does (Theorem 4.17).

statement.name: Open sets given as in (R.2) have a representation as in (R.4)
statement.definition: An open set represented by Y:[0,1]→[0,1] with (x−Y(x),x+Y(x))∩[0,1] ⊆ O whenever Y(x)>0 is a countable union of rational intervals.
statement.facts: RCA0^ω + HBU + QF-AC^{0,1} proves open^- (Theorem 7.8); HBU can be replaced by the Lindelöf lemma for R.

statement.name: Closed sets are located
statement.definition: Any non-empty closed set C ⊆ R (Definition 1.2) is located (d(x,C) exists as a continuous function).
statement.facts: CLO ↔ [ACA0 + open] over RCA0^ω and (∃³) → CLO → HBC (Theorem 4.12); CLO implies BOOT^- + QF-AC^{0,1}_! (Theorem 4.9).

statement.name: Cantor–Bendixson theorem for closed sets given by characteristic functions
statement.definition: Every closed C ⊆ R is P ∪ S with P perfect closed and S a sequence of reals.
statement.facts: CBT implies BOOT^- + QF-AC^{0,1}_! over RCA0^ω (Theorem 4.9).

statement.name: Perfect set theorem for closed sets given by characteristic functions
statement.definition: Every closed uncountable C ⊆ [0,1] has a perfect closed subset P.
statement.facts: RCA0^ω proves PST → BOOT^- (Corollary 4.11). Not the Weihrauch problem PST of the catalogue.

statement.name: Urysohn lemma for closed sets given by characteristic functions
statement.definition: For disjoint closed C0,C1 ⊆ R there is continuous g:R→[0,1] with x ∈ C_i ↔ g(x)=i.
statement.facts: ACA0^ω proves URY ↔ open (Theorem 5.3); RCA0^ω + coco proves URY ↔ open (Corollary 5.4); ACA0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} proves TIE ↔ URY and RCA0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} + coco proves TIE ↔ URY (Theorem 5.6, Corollary 5.7).

statement.name: Tietze extension theorem for closed sets given by characteristic functions
statement.definition: For f:R→R continuous on a closed D ⊆ [0,1] there is g:R→R continuous on [0,1] with f=g on D.
statement.facts: ACA0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} proves TIE ↔ URY, and RCA0^ω proves [TIE + WKL] → HBC (Theorem 5.6); RCA0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} + coco proves TIE ↔ URY (Corollary 5.7).

statement.name: Baire category theorem for open sets given by characteristic functions
statement.definition: If (Y_n) is a sequence of dense open sets of reals (Definition 1.2) then ∩Y_n is non-empty.
statement.facts: RCA0^ω + BOOT proves BCT (Theorem 6.14); RCA0^ω + BOOT_w + coco proves BCT (Corollary 6.15); Z_2^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} does not prove BCT (Theorem 6.16); (∃³) → BCT; BCT → NIN over RCA0^ω (cited from [38]); a Baire realiser is computable in IND and ∃² (Theorem 6.5) but in no type-two functional (Theorem 6.6).

statement.name: Sequential compactness of closed subsets of [0,1] (Definition 1.2)
statement.definition: A closed set in [0,1] is sequentially compact.
statement.facts: RCA0^ω proves ACA0 ↔ this statement; closed sets are sequentially closed in RCA0^ω; ∃² computes an accumulation point (Theorem 3.1).

statement.name: Range principle for functionals G: N^N -> N
statement.definition: (forall G^2)(exists X subset N)(forall n)(n in X <-> (exists f in N^N)(G(f) = n)).
statement.facts: Equivalent to BOOT over RCA_0^omega (proof of Theorem 2.3). Distinct from the catalogue problem 'range' (range of an injection N -> N, second-order).

statement.notation: CLO order-isomorphic to a subset of Q (Cantor)
statement.name: Cantor's characterisation for countable linear orders (CLO, Definition 2.2)
statement.definition: (b) A CLO (X, <=_X) with X subset R (a linear order with Y: R -> N such that Y(x)=Y(y) implies x =_X y) is order-isomorphic to a subset of Q; (c) a CLO without endpoints is order-isomorphic to Q.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1}, (b) and (c) are each equivalent to BOOT (Theorem 2.3). Over ACA_0^omega, the versions with the isomorphism having an inverse (Corollary 2.4(b),(c)) are equivalent to BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1}. For linear orders on countable sets of reals (in the sense (2.2)), the analogous statements are equivalent to cocode0 (Theorem 2.5, over ACA_0^omega, first equivalence cited from Normann-Sanders [36]).

statement.name: Comparability of countable well-orderings in the sense of (2.4)
statement.definition: For cwos (X, <=_X), (Y, <=_Y) with X, Y subset R (well-orderings with a map to N injective modulo =_X), one is order-isomorphic to the other or to an initial segment of it, or vice versa.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} + Sigma-IND, equivalent to BOOT (Theorem 2.7).

statement.notation: Sierpinski's theorem for countable metric spaces
statement.name: Countable metric spaces without isolated points are homeomorphic to Q
statement.definition: Any countable metric space (M,d) with M subset N^N and without isolated points (countable in the sense of Definition 1.1) is homeomorphic to the rationals; the strongly countable version (Definition 2.10) requires Y also surjective onto N.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega, equivalent to BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem 2.9); the strongly countable version is equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1} over ACA_0^omega (Corollary 2.11).

statement.name: Supremum principle for continuous functions on compact CRSC-spaces
statement.definition: For a compact RSC-space X (countable in the sense (2.8)), a continuous f: X -> R and a decreasing sequence (C_n) of closed sets, there is a sequence (x_n) with x_n = sup over C_n of f.
statement.facts: Equivalent to BOOT over ACA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem 2.18), also for scattered CRSC-spaces; the maximum principle (supremum attained) is equivalent to BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1} (remark after Theorem 2.18). Enumerability of scattered RSC-spaces implies BOOT (Corollary 2.19). Different from the catalogue problem 'sup'.

statement.name: Ginsburg-Sands theorem for countable (in the sense (2.8)) RSC-spaces
statement.definition: An infinite CRSC-space has a subspace homeomorphic to the discrete, indiscrete, co-finite, initial segment or final segment topology on N.
statement.facts: Equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1} over ACA_0^omega + IND3 (Theorem 2.21). Third-order version, distinct from the catalogue problem gs (second-order, CSC spaces).

statement.name: Koenig's infinity lemma for finite sets in (X, =_X)
statement.definition: For a sequence (E_n) of finite non-empty sets in (X, =_X) with X subset N^N and a relation R such that every x in E_{n+1} has some y in E_n with yRx, there is a sequence (x_n) with x_n in E_n and x_n R x_{n+1}.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega + IND3, equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1} and to the axiom of finite choice (Principle 2.27) (Theorem 2.28).

statement.name: Axiom of finite choice for finite sets in (X, =_X)
statement.definition: For a sequence (X_n) of finite non-empty sets in (X, =_X) with X subset N^N, there is (x_n) with x_n in X_n for all n.
statement.facts: Equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1} over ACA_0^omega + IND3 (Theorem 2.28); its second-order version finite-Sigma^1_1-AC_0 is strictly weaker than Sigma^1_1-AC_0 (remark after Theorem 2.28).

statement.name: Existence of the range of type-3 functionals
statement.facts: Z2^Ω + QF-AC^{0,2} ⊢ MCT^N_net → RANGE^1 (Corollary 3.9); Z2^Ω ⊢ (item (d)) → RANGE^1 (Corollary 3.15).

statement.name: Monotone convergence theorem for nets in [0,1] indexed by N = N^N → N
statement.definition: Any increasing net in [0,1] indexed by N^N→N converges.
statement.facts: Implies RANGE^1 over Z2^Ω + QF-AC^{0,2} (Corollary 3.9).

statement.notation: Heine-Borel compact complete metric spaces over N^N are totally bounded
statement.name: Compactness of metric spaces over Baire space
statement.definition: (a) A Heine-Borel compact complete metric space over N^N is totally bounded; (b) restricted to countable Heine-Borel compactness; (c) with sequential compactness.
statement.facts: ACA0^ω + IND ⊢ each of (a), (b), (c) → BOOT (Theorem 3.13); ACA0^ω + IND ⊢ (a) → QF-AC^{0,1} (Corollary 3.14). IND (induction for all formulas of L_ω) has no catalogue id.

statement.notation: Maximal ideals of commutative rings / integral domains over N^N
statement.name: Existence of maximal ideals for rings over Baire space
statement.definition: (a) A commutative ring over N^N has a maximal ideal; (b) an integral domain over N^N has a maximal ideal.
statement.facts: Over ACA0^ω either implies BOOT (Theorem 3.41); the proof also applies ∆-CA, which is not listed in the hypothesis.

statement.name: Markov's principle for computations
statement.definition: forall e (not forall s phi_e(0)[s] diverges -> exists s phi_e(0)[s] converges); equivalent to MP restricted to computable sequences (MP^TM, [10]).
statement.facts: MP implies MP^PR clearly (Remark before Observation 7.7); realizability: MP^PR is F-realizable iff Sigma1-C_{1/omega} <=GtW F (Observation 7.7, Theorem 7.8 remark). Separated from WLEM and LLPO (not implied) in models of Theorem 1.1(3),(6),(9); MP^PR + WLEM + not LEM consistent (Theorem 1.1(12)). Not bish: models lack countable choice.

statement.name: n-disjunctive Markov's principle
statement.definition: For alpha in 2^{n x N} with at most one 1 and not all zero, some k<n has alpha_k = 0^infty (MP^v_2 is the catalogue's mpor presumably).
statement.facts: Hierarchy MP^v_{n+1} not implying MP^v_n in modified realizability subtoposes (Theorem 1.1(2),(5),(8)); MP^v_n realizable iff Sigma1-C_{n-1/n} <=GtW F (Theorems 7.5, 7.9). Not bish.

statement.name: Richman's LLPO_n
statement.definition: For alpha in 2^{n x N} with at most one 1, some k<n has alpha_k=0^infty; LLPO = LLPO_2.
statement.facts: LLPO_n realizable iff Pi1-C_{>=n-1/n} <=GtW F (Theorems 7.11, 7.13); LLPO_{n+1} does not imply LLPO_n in a model (Theorem 1.1(7),(10)). Not bish.

statement.name: n-ary weak law of excluded middle
statement.definition: If not (A_k and A_l) for all k<l<n then some k<n has not A_k; WLEM = WLEM_2, WLEM_omega for omega.
statement.facts: WLEM_n realizable iff C_{n-1/n} <=GtW F (Theorem 7.15); hierarchy strict in models (Theorem 1.1(8),(10),(11)). Not bish.

statement.name: De Morgan law on the natural numbers
statement.definition: not forall n A(n) -> exists n not A(n).
statement.facts: Realizable iff C_{1/omega} <=GtW F (Theorem 7.17); fails in the model of Theorem 1.1(12) while WLEM holds, so does not follow from WLEM + MP^PR.

statement.notation: CT_0, CT_0!, wCT_0, nCT_0, CT_0^maj, sCT_0^maj
statement.name: Variants of constructive Church's thesis
statement.definition: CT_0: every total relation on N has a computable choice function (CT_0!: unique); wCT_0 with double negation; nCT_0 for partial relations; majorization versions.
statement.facts: Realizability results in Theorems 7.22-7.34 (e.g. CT_0 is not Sigma1-C_{n-1/n}-realizable, Theorem 7.30; CT_0! not Sigma1-C_{1/2}- or Pi1-C_{>=1/2}-realizable, Theorem 7.31); these are used in the separation models of Theorem 1.1. Catalogue has only the function form CT.

statement.name: Independence of premise
statement.definition: forall x [(not D(x) -> exists y A(x,y)) -> exists y (not D(x) -> A(x,y))].
statement.facts: IP is F-realizable iff F is multi-query total Weihrauch equivalent to a total problem, for F with arithmetical graph (Theorem 7.38); fails for Sigma1-C_{1/omega}, Sigma1-C_{n-1/n} (Corollary 7.40); incompatible with ECT_0 over HA (Fact 3, Troelstra).

statement.name: Functional embodying Π¹₁-comprehension (µ¹)
statement.definition: (∃µ^{1→1})(∀f¹)[(∃g¹)(∀x⁰)(f(ḡx)=0) → (∀x⁰)(f(µ¹(f)x̄)=0)]: selects a witness g for Σ¹₁ formulas in normal form.
statement.facts: RCA₀^ω + QF-AC^{1,1} proves (µ¹) ↔ (S²) (as in [19, Cor. 3.5]); over B₀ + (κ³) (µ¹) ↔ Π¹₁-TRANS (Corollary 4.10); (E²) implies (µ¹).

statement.name: Kohlenbach's functional κ (generalisation of WKL)
statement.facts: RCA₀^ω + (κ³) is conservative over WKL₀; MUC implies (κ³); Kohlenbach: RCA₀^ω proves [(κ³)+(∃²)] → (E²) (type-3 ∃³), Footnote 5; over B₀+(κ³), (µ²) ↔ Π⁰₁-TRANS, (µ¹) ↔ Π¹₁-TRANS, (E²) ↔ SOT (nonstandard).

statement.name: Type-3 search functional µ-style (U³)
statement.facts: (U³) ↔ (E²) over RCA₀^ω + QF-AC^{2,1} (E² is the catalogue's exists3).

statement.name: Fragments of Transfer
statement.definition: Restrictions of Transfer to Π⁰₁-, Π¹₁- and all formulas in the nonstandard system B₀.
statement.facts: Π⁰₁-TRANS ↔ (∃²)-style functional and (µ²) over B₀+(κ³) (Theorems 4.4, 4.8); Π¹₁-TRANS ↔ (µ¹) (Corollary 4.10); (E²) ↔ SOT (Corollary 4.11). Nonstandard systems, no catalogue counterpart.

statement.name: Heine-Borel theorem for uncountable coverings restricted to functions continuous almost everywhere
statement.definition: HBU restricted to Psi : [0,1] -> R+ continuous outside an RM-closed set of measure zero.
statement.facts: Theorem 2.2: RCA0^omega proves HBU <-> HBU_ae. Corollary 2.3 (ACA0^omega): HBU is equivalent to the Heine-Borel theorem for canonical coverings indexed by an RM-closed measure zero set E.

statement.name: WHBU restricted to functions continuous almost everywhere
statement.definition: WHBU for Psi continuous almost everywhere (Definition 2.1).
statement.facts: Theorem 2.5: RCA0^omega + WKL proves WHBU_ae. Corollary 2.6: RCA0^omega proves WWKL <-> WHBU_ae.

statement.name: BOOT restricted to functionals continuous almost everywhere
statement.definition: (exists X subset N)(forall n)(n in X <-> (exists x in [0,1])(Y(x,n)=0)) where lambda x.Y(x,n) is continuous almost everywhere on [0,1] for each n.
statement.facts: Corollary 2.4: RCA0^omega proves BOOT <-> BOOT_ae.

statement.name: Strengthening of the Vitali covering theorem (countable exceptional set)
statement.definition: For Psi : [0,1] -> R+, there is a sequence (y_n) in [0,1] such that [0,1] minus the union of the I^Psi_{y_n} is countable (Definition 1.6).
statement.facts: Theorem 2.9: over RCA0^omega + A0, HBU <-> [WHBU+ + HBC0 + WKL], A0 only needed for HBU -> HBC0. Theorem 2.10: Z_2^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} + WHBU+ cannot prove HBC0; RCA0^omega + HBC0 + WHBU+ cannot prove WKL0. WHBU+ + HBC0 is a conservative extension of RCA0^omega. HBU -> WHBU+ is trivial.

statement.name: Weak HBC0
statement.definition: HBC0 with the conclusion weakened to the existence of a sequence (a_n, b_n) of intervals in A with measure at least one.
statement.facts: (2.6): WHBU <-> [WHBU+ + WHBC0 + WWKL], provable like (2.4) assuming QF-AC^{0,1}. Only remarked, no proof.

statement.name: Finite Choice (axiom of choice for finite sets of reals)
statement.definition: Given a sequence (Xn) of non-empty finite sets in [0,1], there is (xn) with xn ∈ Xn for all n.
statement.facts: Over ACA0^ω+IND2 it follows from items (a)-(j) of Theorem 2.5, items of Theorems 2.6, 2.10, 2.13 (metric space properties), and is implied by QF-AC0,1; it implies finite-Σ11-AC0 over ACA0^ω; Theorem 3.7: QF-AC0,1 → (regulated f with infinite discontinuity set has a sequence of distinct points) → Finite Choice → finite-Σ11-AC0 over ACA0^ω+IND0; Theorem 4.2: ClC → Finite Choice → finite-Σ11-AC0.

statement.name: Height version of finite-Σ11-AC0 and of Finite Choice
statement.definition: finite-Σ11-AC0 with a given height function g bounding the sizes of the finite sets; Finite Choice′ is Finite Choice with |Xn| ≤ g(n).
statement.facts: Σ11-AC0 → finite-Σ11-AC0 → height-Σ11-AC0 → weak-Σ11-AC0; Corollary 3.8 (ACA0^ω): QF-AC0,1 → BV-functions with infinite discontinuity set have a sequence of distinct discontinuities → Finite Choice′ → height-Σ11-AC0; Section 4.2: height-Σ11-AC0 follows from item (ii) of Theorem 4.7.

statement.name: Choice for sequences of non-empty closed sets in [0,1]
statement.definition: For a sequence (Cn) of non-empty closed sets in [0,1] (closed sets as characteristic functions) there is (xn) with xn ∈ Cn.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.2 (ACA0^ω+IND2): QF-AC0,1 → extreme value theorem for usco functions ↔ ClC → (usco and regulated version) → Finite Choice → finite-Σ11-AC0; ClC is provable in WKL0 for sets given by RM-codes.

statement.name: Induction principles on finite sequences of functions
statement.definition: IND2: if for all n there is f ∈ 2^N with Y(f,n)=0 then for every n there is a finite sequence w of length n with Y(i,w(i))=0 for i<n; IND0, IND1 restrict to 'at most one' resp. 'exactly one' f.
statement.facts: Z2^ω+IND2 does not prove that the unit interval is not strongly countable ([52, Theorem 2.16]); used as hypothesis in Theorems 2.5-2.13, 3.5, 3.7, 4.2, 4.7 and Theorem 2.8.

statement.name: Boundedness, uniform continuity, attainment of infimum, Dini, closed map lemma, Cantor intersection, Ascoli-Arzelà, intermediate value theorem on sequentially compact (chain connected) metric spaces M ⊂ R
statement.definition: Third-order versions for arbitrary metric spaces on subsets of R without second-order codes.
statement.facts: Over ACA0^ω+IND2, QF-AC0,1 implies each item and each implies Finite Choice; items (a),(c),(d)-(g) of Theorem 2.13 (intermediate value theorem, approximate IVT, chain connected implies connected, ...) are equivalent; Theorem 2.8: item (a) of Theorem 2.5 for arithmetically defined objects implies weak-Σ11-AC0 over ACA0^ω+IND1.

statement.notation: Jordan decomposition with given total variation
statement.name: Jordan decomposition theorem for f ∈ BV with V01(f)=1 given, and related statements
statement.definition: For f ∈ BV with V01(f)=1 there are non-decreasing g,h with f=g−h; (iii) a sequence containing all discontinuities; (iv) suprema over rational intervals exist.
statement.facts: Over ACA0^ω+IND1: QF-AC0,1 → (ii) ↔ (iii) → (iv) → cocode1 → weak-Σ11-AC0; Corollary 3.6 equivalence with Fourier series convergence outside a sequence; not the catalogue's jordan (total variation is given).

statement.name: Positive convergent unordered sums over [0,1]
statement.definition: Properties: sum has a sequence of reals outside which ax=0; existence of a modulus of convergence.
statement.facts: Over ACA0^ω+IND1: QF-AC0,1 → (ii) ↔ (iii) → cocode1; height-Σ11-AC0 follows from (ii); cocode1 for the enumerable-set versions: Theorem 4.5.

statement.name: Choice of points in sequences of enumerable sets (non-empty / positive measure) in [0,1]; analytic-code versions
statement.definition: (Sn) enumerable non-empty (resp. positive measure) sets in [0,1] have a choice sequence.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.5 (ACA0^ω): QF-AC0,1 → both items → cocode1; Theorem 4.4 (ACA0): analytic-code versions are between Σ11-AC0 and weak-Σ11-AC0.

items.quote: + cocode0 proves ATR0 ([32]) while the latter is
items.concerns: Stated in the proof of Theorem 3.6 with a citation to [32]; the base is ACA_0^omega, hence the conjunct exists2. Overlines/superscripts lost in extraction (ACAω 0).
reasons: attributed by the paper to [32]: cite the original

items.quote: is third-order and weaker than (∃3 ), but we still have that Π1k -CAω
items.concerns: Only the implication (BOOT is weaker than (∃3)) is recorded; the paper does not state strictness here.

statement.notation: boundary/closure/interior existence for closed, open, F_sigma and arbitrary sets
statement.name: Existence of the boundary, closure and interior of sets of reals
statement.definition: For a set of reals given by a representation function, the boundary, closure or interior (Definition 2.1) exists as a set (also with an RM-code, or as an operator (R->R)->(R->R)).
statement.facts: Over RCA_0^omega, the existence of the boundary of closed sets, of open sets, or of a boundary functional is equivalent to (exists^2) (Thm 2.3); closure of open sets and interior of closed sets exist in ACA_0^omega. Over ACA_0^omega+QF-AC^{0,1}, existence of the closure of F_sigma sets (or interior of G_delta sets) implies NIN[0,1] (Thm 2.4); over ACA_0^omega the existence of the closure of F_sigma sets proves ATR_0 and is conservative over it (Thm 2.5). Over ACA_0^omega, BOOT is equivalent to the existence of the interior (or closure) of any set of reals, with or without an RM-code (Thm 2.6); existence of the interior or closure operator is equivalent to (exists^3) (Cor 2.7).

statement.name: Range principle for functionals on Baire space
statement.definition: (for all G: N^N -> N)(exists Z subset N)(for all n)[n in Z <-> (exists f in 2^N)(G(f) = n)].
statement.facts: Equivalent to BOOT (stated 'straightforward', cited to [44, 46]).

statement.name: Range of an injective-on-A functional on a countable set of [0,1]
statement.definition: For countable A subset of [0,1] and Y: [0,1] -> N injective on A, there is X subset N with n in X <-> (exists x in A)(Y(x) = n).
statement.facts: Equivalent to cocode_0 (cited [32, 33]); also equivalent to the 'at most one' comprehension principle for arithmetical phi (and over ACA_0^omega the latter gives ATR_0 by [49, V.5.2]).

statement.name: Enumeration principle for countable unions of finite sets
statement.definition: If A = union over n of finite sets A_n of reals, then A can be enumerated.
statement.facts: Slightly more general than cocode_0; equivalent to it over fairly weak base theories.

statement.name: D-representation of open sets and its principles
statement.definition: A set is D-open if it is a union of sets J_n each an open interval or a union of two open intervals (not decided which); open_D: every D-open set is a union of a sequence of open intervals; open_D^dagger: every D-open set is a countable union of D-closed sets.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega+QF-AC^{0,1}, cocode_0 is equivalent to open_D, to the existence of distance functions and suprema for D-closed sets, to the perfect set theorem for D-closed sets (non-enumerable D-closed set has a perfect D-closed subset), to closure of F_sigma^D sets, to the supremum/maximum principles for D-usco functions, to Urysohn's lemma for D-closed sets, to Tietze plus open_D^dagger, to Lindelof for D-closed sets, and to the supremum principle for continuous functions on D-closed sets (Thm 3.6). Over ACA_0^omega a perfect D-closed set is RM-closed (Thm 3.2); D-continuous equals continuous (Thm 3.4).

statement.name: Third-order Cantor-Bendixson and perfect set theorems with countable sets
statement.definition: CBT: a closed C subset of R is the disjoint union of a perfect closed set and a countable set (injection to N); PST: every uncountable closed set of reals has a perfect subset.
statement.facts: Z_2^omega+QF-AC^{0,1}+CBT+PST does not prove NIN[0,1], and ACA_0^omega+CBT+PST cannot prove ATR_0 (Thm 3.15). The enumerable version of CBT for D-closed sets is equivalent to cocode_0+Pi^1_1-CA_0 (Remark 3.8).

statement.name: Existence of an injection from [0,1] to N
statement.definition: The negation of NIN[0,1]: there is Y: [0,1] -> N injective.
statement.facts: ACA_0^omega + not-NIN[0,1] cannot prove ATR_0 (answering Mummert's question); NIN[0,1] <-> NIN_{2^N} readily proved (cited [39]). The Kleene S1-S9 model of objects computable in (exists^2) satisfies ACA_0^omega + not-NIN + not-ATR_0.

statement.name: Transfer restricted to universal number quantifiers (Nelson's IST fragment)
statement.definition: (∀st f¹)[(∀st n⁰) f(n) ≠ 0 → (∀m) f(m) ≠ 0], in the system P of nonstandard arithmetic.
statement.facts: P ⊢ MCTns ↔ Π⁰₁-TRANS (Theorem D.1); P + Π⁰₁-TRANS proves the existence of the Turing jump ([78, §4.1]).

statement.name: Transfer restricted to Π¹₁ formulas
statement.definition: (∀f¹)[(∃g¹)(∀x⁰)(f(gx)≠0) → (∃st g¹)(∀st x⁰)(f(gx)≠0)], in the system P.
statement.facts: P ⊢ PSTns ↔ Π¹₁-TRANS (Theorem D.4); P ⊢ DIVns → Π¹₁-TRANS (Theorem D.5).

statement.name: Feferman's second mu-operator
statement.facts: Equivalent in uniform form to PST (Theorem D.4) and implied by uniform DIV (Theorem D.5), in E-PA^ω*.

items.quote: since (∃2 ) → ACA0 , we have access to much more powerful tools (than just WKL0 ).
items.argument: Stated in the LEM trick, over RCA0^ω (conservative over RCA0 for second-order ACA0): Kleene's quantifier implies arithmetical comprehension.
items.concerns: ACA0 read as catalogue id aca, which is a problem in the catalogue (alias ACA0); the statement is the axiom ACA0. Third-order hypothesis over RCA0^ω.

items.loc: Section 2.2.1, remark after Theorem 2.12 list (via Theorem 3.12)
items.quote: from the Big Five. For instance, the full Jordan decomposition theorem implies
items.argument: Stated as a consequence of Theorem 3.12 (equivalences over ACA0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1}, enum implies no injection from [0,1] to N via items on Jordan decomposition). Base: ACA0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} given as conjuncts exists2 and qfac01.
items.concerns: The paper only says 'by Theorem 3.12', whose Jordan item (g) is for f:R->R in BV([0,a]) with monotone g,h:R->R, not literally Theorem 2.9. Base ACA0^ω + QF-AC^{0,1} is that of Theorem 3.12, not stated in the sentence. Quote continues on next line with NIN[0,1] by Theorem 3.12.

statement.name: Unit interval not height-width-countable
statement.definition: The unit interval is not height-width-countable (height function H and width function g in N^N with |A_n| <= g(n)).
statement.facts: Equivalent to NINalt over ACA0^ω with relatively weak extra principles, and to most items of Theorems 3.6-3.7 with 'regulated' replaced by 'BV'.

statement.name: Induction axiom for third-order existential formulas
statement.definition: For F:(R x N)->N and k in N there is X subset N with (for all n<=k)((exists x in R)(F(x,n)=0) <-> n in X).
statement.facts: Used as extra base axiom in Theorems 3.23-3.24 and for fragmented/B-measurable variants of BCT[0,1].

items.quote: Each item implies the one below it.
items.paperNotation: Jordan decomposition theorem for the unit interval, over ACA0^omega
items.concerns: Stated over ACA0^omega = RCA0^omega + (E2), hence the conjunct exists2; chain Jordan -> HBU_bv -> NIN, the middle statement (HBU restricted to bounded variation gauges) is not in the catalogue. The catalogue jordan is the theorem for every f of bounded variation on [0,1], matching the paper.

items.quote: NIN follows from HBUsemi and from HBUBorel
items.paperNotation: HBU (Cousin's lemma) restricted to semi-continuous or Borel gauges
items.argument: HBU is the statement for all gauges Psi: R -> R+, so it implies its restrictions HBU_semi and HBU_Borel; Theorem 18 derives NIN from HBU_semi over ACA0^omega + IND0.
items.concerns: The paper says IND0 is needed only for HBU_semi, not HBU_Borel (but the proof of Theorem 15 uses IND0 for Borel functions); IND0 kept as a conjunct to be safe, so the fact is weaker than possibly true. Whether the catalogue hbu is the paper's HBU (gauges Psi: R -> R+, finite subcover of [0,1]) was checked against the definition in Section 2.3.
Both are third-order existence axioms; over RCA0^omega the base is rca0 by the database convention.

statement.name: No injection from Cantor space to N
statement.definition: There is no injection Y: 2^N -> N.
statement.facts: NIN <-> NIN^C <-> NIN^N <-> NIN^R over ACA0^omega (Theorem 6); the Baire-space and real-line versions are NIN^N and NIN^R.

statement.name: No injection from Baire space to N
statement.definition: There is no injection Y: N^N -> N.
statement.facts: Equivalent to NIN over ACA0^omega (Theorem 6).

statement.name: No injection from R to N
statement.definition: There is no injection Y: R -> N.
statement.facts: Equivalent to NIN over ACA0^omega (Theorem 6).

statement.name: No bijection from R (resp. Baire space) to N
statement.definition: There is no bijection from R (resp. N^N) to N.
statement.facts: ACA0^omega proves NBI <-> NBI^R and NBI -> NBI^N; also NBI <-> NBI^{R>=0} (Theorem 8).

statement.name: Enumeration of countable subsets of R / Cantor space
statement.definition: Any (strongly, for i=1) countable subset of R (resp. 2^N) can be enumerated.
statement.facts: Over ACA0^omega, cocode_i^R <-> cocode_i^C <-> cocode_i for i=0,1 (Theorem 7).

statement.notation: NIN_bv, NIN_Riemann, NIN_Borel, NIN_reg, NIN_cliq, NIN_semi, NIN'_semi, NIN_Y
statement.name: NIN restricted to injections [0,1] -> Q of a function class
statement.definition: There is no injection from [0,1] to Q that has bounded variation / is Riemann integrable / Borel / regulated / cliquish / upper (lower) semi-continuous / has a property Y implied by bounded variation.
statement.facts: All equivalent to NIN over ACA0^omega + IND0 (only the last five need IND0).

statement.notation: NBI_Riemann, NBI_bv, NBI_Borel, NBI_cliq, NBI_semi, NBI'_semi
statement.name: NBI restricted to a function class
statement.definition: There is no bijection from [0,1] to Q in the given class (bv: no injection with total variation 1).
statement.facts: All equivalent to NBI over ACA0^omega + IND0 (the last four need IND0).

statement.name: HBU restricted to gauges Psi: [0,1] -> R+ that are upper semi-continuous / Borel / in class B2 / of bounded variation
statement.definition: Cousin's lemma for gauges in the given class.
statement.facts: HBU_semi and HBU_Borel imply NIN over ACA0^omega + IND0 (IND0 only for semi); HBU_B2 -> NIN (Corollary 19); Jordan -> HBU_bv -> NIN over ACA0^omega (Theorem 21).

statement.notation: weak measure zero of countable sets
statement.name: A countable subset of [0,1] has weak measure zero
statement.definition: Footnote 4 defines weak measure zero via a sequence of covering intervals indexed injectively.
statement.facts: Provable in ACA0^omega (Theorem 9).

statement.name: Heine's theorem for separably closed sets (second-order)
statement.definition: For C subset of [0,1] separably closed, any RM-continuous f : C -> R is uniformly continuous with a modulus on C.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.3: ACA0 <-> HEI^2 <-> WEI^2 over RCA0.

statement.name: Weierstrass approximation theorem for separably closed sets (second-order)
statement.definition: For C subset of [0,1] separably closed and RM-continuous f : C -> R, there is a sequence of polynomials p_n with |f(x)-p_n(x)| < 1/2^n on C.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.3: ACA0 <-> HEI^2 <-> WEI^2 over RCA0.

statement.name: Heine's theorem for separably closed sets (third-order)
statement.definition: For C subset of [0,1] separably closed, any f : R -> R continuous on C is uniformly continuous with a modulus on C.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.6: provable in RCA0^omega + WKL; Corollary 3.7: HEI^omega <-> WKL <-> WEI^omega over RCA0^omega.

statement.name: Weierstrass approximation theorem for separably closed sets (third-order)
statement.definition: For C subset of [0,1] separably closed and f : R -> R continuous on C, there is a sequence of polynomials p_n with |f(x)-p_n(x)| < 1/2^n on C.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.6: provable in RCA0^omega + WKL; Corollary 3.7: HEI^omega <-> WKL <-> WEI^omega over RCA0^omega.

statement.name: One-point-extension theorem
statement.definition: If f is RM-continuous from (0,1) to R with lim_{x->+0} f(x)=0, there is RM-continuous f~ on [0,1) extending f with f~(0)=0.
statement.facts: Theorem 2.9: equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (reversal due to Tanaka [76]); the third-order version (Theorem 2.10) is provable in RCA0^omega.

statement.name: Higher-order versions of Ekeland's weak variational principle FVP for total (continuous) potentials
statement.definition: Third-order versions of FVP of Fernandez-Duque, Shafer and Yokoyama [20]: for all f : [0,1] -> R (resp. continuous f) and on Baire space.
statement.facts: Theorem 4.2 and Theorem 4.4: given proofs in ACA0^omega / RCA0^omega + WKL (resp. Z_2^Omega / RCA0^omega + ACA0), the total version is provable in RCA0^omega + WKL (resp. a conservative extension of ACA0); so no higher-order version can imply ACA0 (resp. Pi^1_1-CA0).

items.concerns: Baire 1 = pointwise limit of continuous third-order functions; catalogue entry gives only 'restricted to gauges of Baire class 1' so the definition should be checked. Third-order, over RCA0^omega.

items.concerns: Stated in words ('not provable from WKL and much stronger systems'); over RCA0^omega. The catalogue's hbu is Cousin's lemma for arbitrary Psi.
