items.quote: Cousin’s lemma for usco Ψ : [0, 1] → R+ .
items.paperNotation: Cousin's lemma for usco Psi implies NIN[0,1] over ACA_0^omega + IND_0
items.argument: Theorem 2.34 (over ACA_0^omega + IND_0, ACA_0^omega = RCA_0^omega + (exists^2)) shows that Cousin's lemma for usco Psi : [0,1] -> R+ implies NIN[0,1]. The full Cousin's lemma HBU for arbitrary Psi has this as a special case (restriction to usco gauges).
items.concerns: IND_0 is the paper's Definition 2.29, same as catalogue ind03. Deduction from the restriction; hbu in the catalogue is stated for Psi defined on R.

items.quote: Vitali’s principle for usco Ψ : [0, 1] → R+ .
items.paperNotation: Vitali's principle (WHBU) for usco Psi implies NIN[0,1] over ACA_0^omega + IND_0
items.argument: Corollary 2.35 shows that Vitali's principle for usco Psi implies NIN[0,1] over ACA_0^omega + IND_0. The full Vitali principle (WHBU, arbitrary Psi) has it as a special case.
items.concerns: Catalogue whbu: formulation differs slightly (measure in the comparative sense); check against the paper's displayed Vitali's principle in Section 2.3.3.

items.quote: Jordan decomposition theorem (Theorem 1.4) restricted to usco BV -functions.
items.paperNotation: Jordan decomposition theorem for usco BV functions implies NIN[0,1] over ACA_0^omega + IND_0
items.argument: Theorem 2.37 proves NIN[0,1] over ACA_0^omega + IND_0 from the Jordan decomposition theorem restricted to usco BV functions; the full theorem for all BV functions has this as a special case.
items.concerns: BV is Definition 1.3(a) of the paper.

statement.notation: Boundedness of regulated / usco / cadlag / quasi-continuous functions
statement.name: Boundedness and supremum principles for classes of discontinuous functions on [0,1]
statement.definition: A regulated (or cadlag, or usco, lsco, quasi-continuous, regulated and Baire 1, ...) function F:[0,1]->R is bounded (above/below); a bounded usco function with a supremum attains it; bounded cadlag, quasi-continuous or Baire 1 functions have a supremum (Definitions 1.2).
statement.facts: Over RCA_0^omega + QF-AC^{0,1} (QF-AC^{0,1} not needed for items (xii),(xvi),(xvii),(xx)-(xxiv)), each of the 24 items of Theorem 2.9 is equivalent to WKL. Items (ix),(x),(xviii),(xix) are provable in RCA_0^omega + Sigma^1_1-AC_0 (Remark 2.10).

statement.notation: Cousin's lemma for regulated, lsco, quasi-continuous, cadlag functions
statement.name: Cousin's lemma for restricted classes of gauges
statement.definition: Cousin's lemma (finite sub-covering of [0,1] by balls B(x,Psi(x))) for gauges Psi:[0,1]->R+ that are lsco, quasi-continuous, cadlag, regulated with F(x)=(F(x-)+F(x+))/2, etc.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL over RCA_0^omega (Theorem 2.14 (iii)-(xii)); for usco, cliquish, BV, regulated, Baire 1*, Baire 2 gauges Cousin's lemma implies NIN[0,1] (Theorem 2.34) over ACA_0^omega + IND_0.

statement.notation: Vitali's principle for classes of gauges
statement.name: Vitali's principle (WHBU-type) for continuous, lsco, cadlag, Baire 1 ... gauges
statement.definition: For Psi:[0,1]->R+ and eps>0 there are x_0..x_k such that the union of B(x_i,Psi(x_i)) has measure 1-eps, restricted to a class of gauges.
statement.facts: Theorem 2.15: over RCA_0^omega each version (continuous, lsco, quasi-continuous, cadlag, Baire 1, ...) is equivalent to WWKL. Corollary 2.35: the versions for BV, regulated, usco, cliquish, Baire 1*, Baire 2 gauges imply NIN[0,1] over ACA_0^omega + IND_0.

statement.name: Jordan decomposition theorem for cadlag (or quasi-continuous) BV functions
statement.definition: A cadlag BV function f:[0,1]->R is the difference of two non-decreasing functions (also for BV functions with f(x)=(f(x+)+f(x-))/2, and quasi-continuous BV functions).
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA_0 over RCA_0^omega (+IND_2 for the second and third versions). Theorem 2.16: ACA_0^omega proves that for regulated f there is a sequence containing all jump discontinuities. Restricted to usco BV functions it implies NIN[0,1] (Theorem 2.37).

statement.notation: Supremum principle for effectively Baire n functions
statement.name: Supremum of bounded effectively Baire 2 (n>=2) functions
statement.definition: A bounded effectively Baire n function f:[0,1]->R has a supremum.
statement.facts: Over ACA_0^omega equivalent to: every bounded Sigma^1_{1,x}-class in Q+ has a supremum; assuming IND_2 + Sigma^1_1-IND equivalent to Pi^1_1-CA_0. Baire 2 / Baire 1* / cliquish / regulated / usco / BV versions (Principle 2.31) imply NIN[0,1] over ACA_0^omega + IND_0 (Theorem 2.32).

statement.notation: Cousin's lemma for effectively Baire n functions
statement.name: Cousin's lemma for effectively Baire n gauges (n>=2)
statement.definition: Cousin's lemma for gauges Psi:[0,1]->R+ that are effectively Baire n.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR_0 over ACA_0^omega + Delta^1_2-IND, as is Cousin's lemma for codes for Baire 2 functions (from Barrett–Downey–Greenberg [6,7]).

statement.notation: Jordan decomposition and enumeration of discontinuities for arithmetical/Sigma^1_1 BV functions
statement.name: Enumerating discontinuities of BV functions
statement.definition: For arithmetical (or Sigma^1_1) f:[0,1]->R in BV there is a sequence enumerating all points of discontinuity; Jordan decomposition for arithmetical (Sigma^1_1) BV functions; a non-enumerable arithmetical set in R has a limit point.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR_0 over ACA_0^omega + IND_2 + Sigma^1_2-IND (Theorem 2.25); for Baire 1 BV functions provable from ATR_0 plus induction (Theorems 2.26, 2.27).

statement.notation: Existence of a non-Riemann-integrable / non-regulated / non-Baire 1 / non-usco / non-quasi-continuous / non-cliquish / unbounded function
statement.name: Existence of wild third-order functions
statement.definition: E.g. there is a function f:[0,1]->R that is not Baire 1; there are Riemann integrable f,g such that g o f is not Riemann integrable; there is a bounded Darboux function not attaining its sup; a code for a Baire 1 function denotes a third-order function.
statement.facts: Each of the 17 items is equivalent to (exists^2) over RCA_0^omega + WKL (WKL needed only for items (i),(ii),(xi),(xii),(xv)).

statement.notation: All BV / regulated / usco functions are Baire 1
statement.name: Inclusions among function spaces (BV, regulated, usco, Baire 1*, Baire 2, effectively Baire n)
statement.definition: E.g. 'all usco (or lsco) functions f:[0,1]->R are Baire 1', 'all Baire 1* functions are Baire 1', 'there is a function [0,1]->R not Baire 2'.
statement.facts: Each implies NIN[0,1] over ACA_0^omega + IND_0 (items (xi)-(xv) over ATR_0 + Delta^1_2-IND), hence is not provable in Z_2^omega.

statement.name: Zero of Riemann integrable BV function with integral 0; differentiability point of BV function; continuity point of regulated / usco function
statement.definition: For Riemann integrable BV f:[0,1]->[0,1] with integral 0 there is x with f(x)=0; for f in BV there is a point of differentiability; for regulated (usco) f there is a point of continuity.
statement.facts: Each implies NIN[0,1] over ACA_0^omega + IND_0 (the first, for Baire 1 BV, is provable from ATR_0 plus induction by Theorem 2.27).

statement.name: Convergence of bounded monotone sequences (function parameter-free schematic form)
statement.definition: PCM(f): if f codes a decreasing sequence of reals in [0,1] then it converges with a modulus of convergence (PCM_ar: without modulus); PCM^- is the schema over instances given by terms without function parameters.
statement.facts: Over EA^2 + AC^{0,0}-qf, PCM^- is equivalent to Pi01-CA^- (Corollary 5.7); PRA^2_- + PCM^- contains PRA + Sigma01-IA (Theorem 1.2); PRA^2 + PCM^- proves the Ackermann function total (Corollary 5.9); PRA^2 + AC^{0,0}-qf + WKL does not prove PCM^- (Corollary 1.8).

statement.name: Function parameter-free Pi01 comprehension and choice schemata
statement.definition: Schemata of Pi01 comprehension, resp. choice, for quantifier-free matrices without function parameters.
statement.facts: Over PRA^2 + AC^{0,0}-qf, Pi01-CA^- is equivalent to the d-form of Pi01-AC^- (Lemma 4.1); PRA^2 + AC^{0,0}-qf + Pi01-CA^- contains PRA + Sigma02-IA (Proposition 4.4).

items.quote: (∃2 ) → ACA0 , we have access to much more powerful tools (than just WKL0 ).
items.concerns: Stated in passing in the proof sketch of the law-of-excluded-middle trick; ACA0 is the second-order sentence (catalogue aca has alias ACA0 but is listed as a problem); over RCA_0^omega.

statement.name: Finite version of QF-AC^{0,1}
statement.definition: For quantifier-free phi with (forall n)(exists f in N^N) phi(f,n), for every k there is a sequence (f_n) with (forall n<=k) phi(f_n,n). Follows from QF-AC^{0,1} (and from the induction axiom).
statement.facts: Used as a side hypothesis in Theorems 2.4, 2.12, 3.6 (equivalences with QF-AC^{0,1}, QF-AC^{0,1->1}).

statement.name: Quantifier-free countable choice for functions Baire to Baire
statement.definition: For quantifier-free phi with (forall n^0)(exists Y^{1->1}) phi(Y,n), there is a sequence (Y_n) with (forall n) phi(Y_n,n).
statement.facts: Theorem 3.6 (over ACA_0^omega): equivalent to the combination of its finite version with sequentially compact implies bounded / countably compact / intermediate value theorem / continuous functions bounded, for M a subset of N = Baire to Baire maps.

statement.name: Generalised bootstrap principles
statement.definition: BOOT2: for Y:(N^N x N^N)->N there is X with n in X iff (exists f)(forall g)(Y(f,g,n)=0); BOOT_k has k-1 quantifier alternations.
statement.facts: BOOT2 implies Pi^1_1-CA_0 over RCA_0^omega, ACA_0^omega+BOOT2 proves Pi^1_2-CA_0 (stated without proof); the supremum principle 2.14 implies BOOT_k (Theorem 2.16, Corollary 2.17, over ACA_0^omega + Sigma-IND).

statement.name: Fourth-order bootstrap principle
statement.definition: (forall Z^3)(exists f^1)(forall n)[f(n)=0 <-> (exists Y in N)(Z(Y,n)=0)] where N is the collection of Baire-to-Baire maps.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.3 (over Z_2^Omega): equivalent to the supremum principle 3.2 for continuous f:M->[0,1] on sequentially compact M = N.

statement.name: Supremum principles for sequentially compact metric spaces on Baire space
statement.definition: Continuous (Lipschitz) functions on sequentially compact metric spaces (M,d), M subset of Baire space, have a supremum as a sequence (2.8, 2.9) or as a function (2.14).
statement.facts: Theorem 2.11 (ACA_0^omega+Sigma-IND): 2.8 and 2.9 restricted to [0,1]-valued functions are equivalent to BOOT. Corollary 2.13: BOOT+QF-AC^{0,1} iff QF-AC^{0,1}_fin + 2.9. Theorem 2.16: 2.14 implies BOOT2. Theorem 2.19: the supremum functional is equivalent to (exists^3) together with (exists^2).

statement.notation: compact metric spaces are separable; sequentially compact implies bounded
statement.name: Metric-space statements without codes
statement.definition: For metric d on N^N x N^N, sequentially compact (M,d) is separable / bounded / countably compact.
statement.facts: Separability implies BOOT and QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem 2.2, ACA_0^omega+Sigma-IND); boundedness (with QF-AC^{0,1}_fin) is equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1} (Theorem 2.4, ACA_0^omega).

statement.name: Open sets in sequentially compact metric spaces are countable unions of open balls
statement.definition: Open sets (resp. with continuous modulus, with R2-representation) of a sequentially compact (M,d), M subset of Baire space, are countable unions of open balls.
statement.facts: Theorem 2.24: each implies BOOT + QF-AC^{0,1} over ACA_0^omega+Sigma-IND.

statement.notation: countable sets can be enumerated; measure zero
statement.name: Countable and measure zero sets in metric spaces
statement.definition: Countable (injective Y on A) sets in metric spaces on Baire space can be enumerated / are effectively measure zero.
statement.facts: Theorem 2.6: the enumeration and effectively-measure-zero statements are equivalent to BOOT+QF-AC^{0,1} (ACA_0^omega+Sigma-IND); Theorem 2.7: for strongly countable sets they are equivalent to QF-AC^{0,1} (ACA_0^omega).

statement.name: Intermediate value theorem on sequentially compact chain connected metric spaces
statement.definition: Continuous f on a sequentially compact chain connected (M,d) with f(w)<c<f(v) takes the value c.
statement.facts: Equivalent (with the finite choice axiom) to QF-AC^{0,1->1} for M subset of N (Theorem 3.6, ACA_0^omega), to QF-AC^{0,1} for M subset of N^N (Corollary 3.7).

items.quote: of IVT has a computable solution while WKL is not so.
items.argument: Stated for computable instances; read as computable truth (relativizes).
items.concerns: Stated for computable instances only; relativization not spelled out.

statement.notation: total ordering of the reals (x ≤ y ∨ y < x)
statement.name: Total ordering of the reals
statement.definition: For all real numbers x, y, x ≤ y or y < x. Used as the example of an instance reduction: given a binary sequence α, build the real x = lim 2^{-min{k | αk=1 or k=n}} and decide x ≤ 0 or 0 < x.
statement.facts: The paper states (1.1) that the total ordering of reals implies LPO (constructively, via an instance reduction). The principle has no catalogue id, so the fact (over bish) is not entered.
